name: Norma
introduction: is the Carpenter’s Square, introduced by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in the 1750s. It is a small, faint constellation in the southern Milky Way between Scorpius and Centaurus.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Norma has lost stars over time: its original Alpha and Beta were reassigned to Scorpius, so Norma’s brightest star is [Gamma² Normae](hip:80000), an orange giant.
In this direction, hidden behind the Milky Way, lies the Norma Cluster of galaxies, near the Great Attractor, a vast concentration of mass pulling our galaxy and its neighbors.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Gamma² Normae](hip:80000) is about 140 light-years away. [Epsilon Normae](hip:80582) is a blue-white multiple star.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The open cluster NGC 6087 contains the Cepheid variable S Normae.
